summary: At segment 0 step 62, a woken hostile leprechaun reaches the incoming AD_SGLD attack and should transfer gold from the hero. C calls steal.c:stealgold after hitmsg(), the same-species guard, and the attacker-canceled guard; JS leaves note_unported("steal.c stealgold") in that exact mhitm_ad_sgld branch. The first divergence is the carried-gold subset draw: C calls somegold(money_cnt(invent)) and records rn2(501)=353, while JS records an unrelated rn2(3)=2 and does not transfer the purse. Implement the contiguous steal.c helper family somegold/findgold/stealgold and wire its existing AD_SGLD and fountain-dip callers.

source.branch: For an uncanceled AD_SGLD attacker hitting the hero, uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_sgld emits hitmsg(), returns for same-species combat, then calls stealgold(). stealgold prefers floor gold when it is available and wins its quantity/random comparison; otherwise, if the hero carries a GOLD_PIECE stack, it calls somegold(money_cnt(invent)), converts the returned value to coins, transfers that quantity, prints the purse-lighter message, teleports/flees when allowed, and sets disp.botl. somegold() uses the source bracket thresholds and rn1 calls, so its selected range also includes the existing findgold() helper in definition order.
callers: uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping dispatches AD_SGLD to mhitm_ad_sgld; mhitu.c:mattacku reaches hitmu, whose AD_SGLD path uses that shared dispatcher before calling steal.c:stealgold.
fountain.c:dipfountain case 28 calls steal.c:somegold to determine the coin loss; js/fountain.js previously kept a private copy rather than using the steal.c owner.
steal.c:relobj releases a vault guard gold stack through findgold(), obj_extract_self(), and obfree(); js/steal.js previously stopped on isgd without checking for gold.
dependencies: Existing JS helpers cover findgold, money_cnt, object extraction/splitting, inventory transfer, monster inventory transfer, message/display, teleport restriction, relocation, and monster fleeing; preserve their source order and thread the existing state/random/message environment through the new owner. The steal.c:relobj caller also needs its existing findgold refusal removed.

The v43 recording proves the carried-gold somegold/stealgold branch. The separate floor-gold snatch branch has source-pinned tests but no matching C recording that reaches it. The committed blocked recipe records the source-based setup barrier in monmove.c:leppie_avoidance.

evidence: The v43 baseline queue SHA-256 1d8802a0f215249923602217eab5fcec9b1d8c57311d4e82b20e23c60140a093 records 15 remaining screens for this case; challenges/evaluations/v43-baseline-d89e1af6.json pins the first mismatch at zero-based segment 0 step 62 (key "l"), call 2110: C rn2(501)=353 from somegold(steal.c:27), JS rn2(3)=2, with C cursor [54,0,1] and JS cursor [45,16,1].

The admitted v43 source trace states that the hero's prior hit wakes the hostile leprechaun; its next attack enters mhitu.c:mattacku -> hitmu -> uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping(AD_SGLD) -> mhitm_ad_sgld -> steal.c:stealgold. At uhitm.c:2815-2821 C performs hitmsg, same-species return, then the !magr->mcan stealgold call; at the inspected baseline, js/uhitm.js:mhitm_ad_sgld replaced that call with note_unported("steal.c stealgold").

Upstream steal.c:14-34 defines somegold’s bounded int conversion and six rn1 brackets; steal.c:45-52 defines findgold; steal.c:58-116 implements floor-stack preference, carried-gold subset and split, ownership transfer, feedback, optional relocation/fleeing, and botl update. The active steal.c:relobj findgold caller had a stale isgd-only refusal; this task wires its source guard, message, extraction, and freeing without claiming unrelated relobj behavior.

The source call sites are distinct and both must remain wired: uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_sgld calls stealgold at 2821, and fountain.c:dipfountain case 28 calls somegold at 510. at the inspected baseline, js/fountain.js:919-942 duplicated somegold privately for dipfountain; centralize it in js/steal.js and import the single owner from fountain.js.

Prior mismatch reports do not cover this behavior: investigations/synthetic/v19/leprechaun-steals-carried-gold-c62.json confirms the sleeping leprechaun never wakes or reaches AD_SGLD/stealgold; investigations/synthetic/v33/v33-leprechaun-hero-gold-steal.json covers the reverse direction (hero leprechaun attacks a no-gold dwarf) and documents the missing stealgold call as a discarded void-call gap; neither exercises successful incoming carried-gold theft.

The current report selects steal.c:somegold/findgold/stealgold and the active callers uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_sgld, fountain.c:dipfountain, and steal.c:relobj. It does not claim unrelated steal.c functions as complete. The v43 replay exercises the carried-gold branch. A separate floor-gold recording is still missing; the blocked recipe names monmove.c:leppie_avoidance as the source barrier when the hero carries no gold.

recipes/steal.c/stealgold-floor-gold-blocked-leppie-avoidance.session.json and its recording match fresh C/JavaScript replay but do not exercise stealgold. C monmove.c:leppie_avoidance makes a leprechaun carrying more gold than the hero avoid the hero; the probe drops all hero gold before creating the leprechaun.
